description: Round 2 role_professional: solid voice answers with quantified results; both critical dimensions should pass.

evidence_items.question_summary: Design an offline warehouse layering scheme for one billion events per day; explain each layer and the trade-offs.
evidence_items.answer_text: ODS ingests raw events to keep replay capability. DWD cleans and standardizes schemas, partitioned by event time. DWS does light subject aggregation to control data growth.ADS serves reporting. Trade-off: DWS granularity sacrifices some detail flexibility for query cost; I chose event time over ingestion time so late events land in correct partitions.

evidence_items.question_summary: Follow-up: how exactly do you handle late-arriving events?
evidence_items.answer_text: A bounded out-of-orderness window: inside the window we backfill the event-time partition; beyond it, events go to a side table merged by a daily compensation job, and the compensation rule is documented downstream.

evidence_items.question_summary: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a teammate at Novalake Analytics.
evidence_items.answer_text: My mentor wanted to add a column for backward compatibility directly; I argued for documenting field semantics first. We compromised: wrote the semantics doc, shipped his approach, and I owned regression verification.

description: Text-mode round: oral_delivery must be not_evaluated (never 0); communication normalizes to structure_clarity.

evidence_items.question_summary: Walk me through the data sync project on your resume.
evidence_items.answer_text: Situation: our team owned daily order sync into the warehouse. Task: I took over dedup and latency. Action: unified field semantics across three upstream tables, rewrote dedup in Python, split the serial job into four parallel shards. Result: P95 latency dropped from ~40 to ~8 minutes, zero failures in two months.
